stem: Mohan cuts a paper parallelogram into pieces $T$ and $U$ and rearranges them into a new outline with no gaps and no overlaps. The diagram shows the original parallelogram and the rearranged outline.

parts.text: Which claim about the areas is correct?

options.text: The rearranged outline has the same area as the original parallelogram.
The new outline must have smaller area because its outer path looks different.
Equal area is what forces the rearranged outline to be a parallelogram again.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Cutting and rearranging with no gaps and no overlaps keeps all of $T$ and $U$, so the area stays the same even though the outline changes.

teacher.key_rationale: Rearrangement with no gaps or overlaps preserves equal area. Treating a different outline as smaller omits that pieces are fully kept. Saying equal area forces a parallelogram again reverses the relation.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as a parallelogram cut into T and U beside a rearranged outline.
